purpose: revised corpus binding decision after d024 low-confidence contradicted result

arguments.decision: How should corpus-mode verifiers establish completeness and bind files to the archive baseline, given that d024 selected the manifest-hash option at confidence 0.41 with a contradicted requirement check?
arguments.evidence: New measurement: format_contracts.archive(HDR, DAT) on the real corpus takes 0.4 seconds and returns, for all 990 files, the archive path (exact case with ;1 suffix), output_bytes and output_sha256. HDR and DAT are already pinned by corpus_identity() baseline hashes, so these per-file values derive from the pinned baseline, not from notes/extracted-manifest.tsv (an unpinned historical file whose binding to the baseline is only checked by the milestone coverage() call). The d024 contradiction: the manifest sha1 prefix check does not bind files to the archive baseline. Review finding: a mirror with 10 .ptg files removed passed. Milestone issue #2: missing required evidence is incomplete; unsupported items listed; complete corpus accounted for; each check independently runnable.
arguments.priorities: Independent binding to the archive baseline; no hard-coded counts that can drift; missing expected files are incomplete, hash or pairing mismatches are fail; reasonable runtime; smallest correct change shared by the three verifiers.

candidates.description: Add a shared corpus_binding module: after corpus_identity(), read HDR/DAT, call archive() and take the expected files for each verifier from the archive entries by suffix (case-insensitive) with their exact paths and output_sha256; missing expected files make the run incomplete; a file whose SHA-256 differs from the archive's fails; unpaired headers or payloads fail; the real-corpus tests still assert the known counts.
Check each file's sha1 prefix against notes/extracted-manifest.tsv plus hard-coded counts.
Investigate more before changing the verifiers.

requirements: The expected set and hashes derive from the pinned baseline (HDR/DAT), not from an unpinned file or constants.
Removing or altering a corpus file cannot yield pass.
